dedupe_keys.name: waste flow european waste data preparation

description: waste_flow is a Python package by Lucas Sinclair and contributors for retrieving and analysing European waste-management statistics. It parses Eurostat waste-generation and treatment tables, distinguishes waste categories and economic activities, and converts wet mass to dry mass using configurable coefficients. Users select countries, years and waste classes; outputs include analysis DataFrames and comparative plots. Geographic and temporal coverage follow the upstream Eurostat tables, with country-level detail, not individual facility flows. Public source and package installation are free under MIT. A limitation is that coefficient choices and custom category mappings affect derived dry-mass totals, and the first run automatically retrieves source files and establishes a local cache. The package depends on Eurostat availability and does not independently verify reported quantities. It can prepare waste-load and treatment inputs for infrastructure capacity simulations, complementary to SwolfPy (model-swolfpy). The README supplies executable usage examples and identifies both upstream table codes. No package was imported and no statistical files or cache repository were downloaded.
